pages.text: What can an anomaly do? The catalogue so far:$(li)break a symmetry and stay broken (defects)$(li)make itself from its surroundings (autocatalysis, prions)$(li)override the rules of its host (oncogenesis)$(li)defy prediction (chaos, undecidability)$(li)copy itself and escape (replicators, metastasis)$(li)evolve resistance$(li)spread through a population$(li)break a conservation law locally$(li)turn partner.

How big do they get? Sizes of tumours, outbreaks, earthquakes, forest fires and ruptures follow $(thing)power laws$(), p(s) ∝ s^{−τ}: most are tiny, a few are enormous, and nothing sets a typical size. The mean is s₀(τ − 1)/(τ − 2) - and for τ ≤ 2 it is infinite: the largest anomaly you will ever meet outweighs all the others together. Systems tuned to the edge of a phase transition do this by themselves (self-organised criticality).
The $(item)Anomaly Containment Ward$() binds one of every kind you have made into the $(item)Anomaly Catalogue$().
Every kind of anomaly you have contained, what it can do, how far it can spread and how big the largest one will be. Most are small; a few are not.$(br2)Made in $(item)Anomaly Containment Ward$().
